newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Zhelev slams cabinet for bringing Bulgaria to ruin.
newsitem.headline: Zhelev slams cabinet for bringing Bulgaria to ruin.

text.p: Bulgarian president Zhelyu Zhelev, a staunch anti-communist, slammed the socialist cabinet of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov in a dramatic late-night television address for bringing the country to economic collapse.
"The reason for this address is the catastrophic state to which Bulgaria was led by the socialist government of Mr. Zhan Videnov," said Zhelev late on Saturday.
Videnov's cabinet took office in January 1995, one month after the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), composed largely of communists, had swept to victory in general elections.
Yet their policies have failed to rescue a national economy now battered by massive inflation and a collapse of confidence in local banks and the national currency, the lev.
Monthly inflation in July hit an all-time high of 23 percent and the central bank's interest rate is a record 108 percent.
A grain crisis caused by excessive exports last year and a poor harvest this year has produced bread queues unprecedented since the Second Warld War.
Trying to battle a fodder shortage, the government recently urged farmers to slaughter swine and poultry in a bid to preserve more valuable cattle.
"Mr. Videnov, please explain to the Bulgarian people how come, after a very good harvest last year, the country is left without bread and fodder?" said Zhelev in his television address.

"Why did your government allow the export of one million tonnes of grain last year without securing the wheat and fodder balance for the population? In whose pockets did the billions of levs profit from these sales sink?".
Hikes in prices of electricity, heating and other utilities have made them unaffordable for many Bulgarians.
"Explain to the millions of pensioners and those working for average state salaries how they and their families will survive," the president went on.
"If people start dying from cold and starvation this winter, responsibility will be sought not only through resignations, but also through the courts," he added.
Zhelev also accused Videnov of evading responsibility and resorting to "cheap propaganda".
In a recent speech Videnov had blamed private businessmen for most of the country's woes.
"These words (Videnov's speech) sound like lines from the darkest years of Stalinism," said Zhelev.
Zhelev, who lost to a little-known lawyer, Petar Stoyanov, in a ground-breaking presidential primary vote in June, is due to step down after the October 27 presidential election.
